sources.identity: David Perkins, Animal Rights and Auguries of Innocence, Blake/An Illustrated Quarterly 33.1 (Summer 1999), 4-11

sources.identity: Michael Srigley, The Sickness of Blake's Rose, Blake/An Illustrated Quarterly 26.1 (Summer 1992), 4-8
sources.bounds: Complete article body, anchors p4-p8, through final note 27
sources.limits: Paracelsus, Vaughan, archival catalogues and proposed channels of transmission not independently read or proved; no adoption of historical medical claims
sources.use: Counterreading of the Sick Rose worm through fantasy and sexual repression; explicitly conjectural source relation.

sources.identity: Robert N. Essick and Joseph Viscomi, An Inquiry into William Blake's Method of Color Printing, Blake/An Illustrated Quarterly 35.3 (Winter 2002), 74-103
sources.bounds: Complete selected prose blocks 6-8, 10-12, 51-54 in readings/essick-viscomi-paragraphs.json (#core h2/h3/p sequence, 1-based): opening pp74-75; Background and Context opening; bottom-sheet registration and cropping/matting discussion pp90-92
sources.limits: Not complete 30-page article; no independent assessment of printing experiments, embedded photographs, or the entire two-pull debate
sources.use: Distinguish colored impressions from color prints; cropping and mounting can conceal artifact relations.

sources.identity: Caroline Dauphin, A Genealogy of the Polypus, from William Blake to H.P. Lovecraft: The Root of All Evil?, Lectures du monde anglophone 7 (2026)
sources.bounds: Numbered paragraphs 7-28, including six intervening quotation blocks; additionally paragraphs 49-50 read in the full prose projection
sources.advance: Extends earlier paragraphs 3-6 and 21-25; overlap explicitly retained, not counted as wholly new reading
sources.limits: No complete article, Lovecraft/Culbard image, thesis, Schwartz chapter, or other cited-book reading credit. No adoption of the article's broad Bible/bestiary or visual absence claims
objections: Article note 9 attributes A Blake Dictionary to David Erdman; this packet does not propagate that attribution (the standard author is S. Foster Damon).
Do not turn claimed Darwin-Blake confluence into proof of one direct source for each passage.
Paragraphs 49-50 do not establish an exhaustive absence of Polypus images in this packet.
sources.use: Generation, bodily boundaries and loss of individuality as a proposed genealogy.

sources.identity: Patricia Fara, Questions of inheritance: Erasmus and Charles Darwin, Romanticism and Victorianism on the Net 66-67 (issue labelled Spring-Fall 2016; online 2020-06-10)
sources.bounds: Complete numbered paragraphs 15-23, printed article pp8-12 (PDF pages 9-13 including cover); first paragraph/title and abstract also checked; paragraph 24 only inspected partly and not admitted
sources.limits: No full article; no full Charles Darwin notebooks, Malthus, Paley or cited books reading; argument about family transmission not adopted
sources.use: Erasmus's insect kinship, predation and material ethics; distinguish the two Darwins and issue/online dates.

sources.identity: William Gould, An Account of English Ants (London: A. Millar, 1747), CUL-DAR.LIB.233
sources.bounds: Title page verified; printed pp66-68 (PDF 82-84), pp78-81 (PDF 94-97), complete pages; ends before p82 continuation
sources.limits: OCR has long-s and recognition errors; no quoted diplomatic transcription; no full book or documented Blake reading/influence
sources.use: Public care moralization alongside repeated observation and correction of English winter-granary narratives.

sources.identity: Henry Baker, The Microscope Made Easy, second edition (London: R. Dodsley, 1743), ESTC T89680; Wellcome EPB/B/11985, b20642659
sources.bounds: Printed pp53-58, scans 0090-0095. Complete paragraphs from 'The Transparency or Opakeness' on p53 through the animalcule dilution paragraph ending 'their true Shape' p58. The incoming continuation at top p53 and outgoing 'But' at foot p58 are not complete reading units
sources.selection_sha_policy: Exact scanned page bytes and first/last paragraph locators bind the selection; no OCR text masquerades as a diplomatic transcription
sources.advance: New actual page-image reading after unsuccessful OCR endpoints
sources.limits: No full chapter/book; no demonstration that Blake read Baker; historical husbandry/observation prescriptions not endorsed as current practice
sources.visual_inspection: All six scans individually opened with view_image; scan0071 only a discovery reverse/foldout and excluded from admitted text bounds
sources.use: Lighting, observer fallibility, projected images, minimal disturbance and restraint.

sources.identity: Erasmus Darwin, Zoonomia vol.I, second edition corrected (London: J. Johnson, 1796), Gutenberg 15707
sources.bounds: Section XXXIX.II.3 in full (five paragraphs) and XXXIX.IV.2 in full (eight paragraphs), including tadpole/gnat/polypus paragraph and concluding paragraph before IV.3
sources.limits: This is the 1796 second edition, not the 1794 first edition; dedication is dated 1794. No causal inference about Blake's 1795 work from this later witness; historical male-only theory not modern biology
sources.use: Budding, separation, development and sexual difference in a historical physiological framework.

sources.identity: Erasmus Darwin, The Temple of Nature (London: J. Johnson, 1803), Gutenberg 26861
sources.bounds: Canto III lines 411-434 (printed pp118-120), Canto IV lines 1-66 (printed pp129-134). No new reading credit for other cantos or Additional Notes
sources.limits: Not complete poem/book; no claim that Darwin's creature identifications or natural-history assertions are modern results
sources.use: Kinship with emmets and worms beside predation across animal and plant life.
